newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-CAMPORESE GIVES ITALY 1-0 LEAD OVER SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CAMPORESE GIVES ITALY 1-0 LEAD OVER SPAIN.

text.p: Veteran Omar Camporese came from two sets down to give Italy a surprise 1-0 lead over Spain in their Davis Cup world group quarter-final on Friday.
Camporese, ranked 156th, lost two tie-breaks to world number eight Carlos Moya before battling to win 6-7 (8-10) 6-7 (4-7) 6-1 6-3 6-3.
Italian number one Renzo Furlan was playing Alberto Costa in the second singles match.
Camporese, 29, showed visible signs of pressure in the first set tie-break against Moya and wasted two set points, the first on a lame double fault.

The 6,000 strong Italian crowd in the indoor arena vented their frustration at the umpire and cried out "shame" after an angry Camporese contested a series of close baseline calls in the highly-charged first tie-break.
Moya said he thought he would win handily after the second tie-break when the crowd fell silent.
"I won the first two sets easily...but after the fourth I began to think I'd lose. Things happen that way in the Davis Cup," the Spaniard said.
But Moya, beaten finalist at this year's Australian Open, never showed the tennis he is capable of and relied instead on unforced errors from the Italian to build his lead.
At the start of the third set Camporese gestured to the crowd for more support and won it 6-1, scoring the first service break by either player after two hours and three minutes.
His confidence high, Camporese then repeatedly hit the baseline with his drives as he raced through the final two sets against a lacklustre Moya.
"I had nothing to lose," a tearful Camporese said. "In front of me I had the world number eight. He had things to worry about."
Moya denied he had taken the game too easily after comments in the Italian press that Italy had no chance of victory.
"You have to take the Davis Cup seriously. Only the Italian press said Spain had an 80 percent chance of victory," he said.
After an elbow injury in 1993, Camporese slid down the world rankings from 18 to his current spot and was written off before the match by the Italian media.
He came off for treatment for cramp in the fourth set, but hung on to the end of the three-hour 42-minute contest.
